title: Annie Hall
about: A neurotic comedian looks back on his relationship with the free-spirited Annie.
cue: Serve the mains when the lobsters escape behind the fridge.
faces: Sweet meat folded with mayonnaise, lemon, celery and chives on toasted, buttered brioche. By the dozen.
Corned beef, pastrami, turkey and tongue, sliced thin. Serves ten.
Out east for the weekend? Trays packed on ice, bread wrapped apart.
Two regulars, on a terrace up the block.
Central Park to the river. Minimum order 5.00. Allow 30 minutes, longer when it rains. Cash only.
Open seven days, 7 A.M. to 1 A.M.
The food is good. The plates are full.
Our first counter, under the coaster at Coney Island, 1946. We came uptown in 1959.
Steamed until glossy, piled high on soft white bread with mayonnaise, iceberg and tomato.
Yes, we make it. Max winces.
Garlic cured brisket carved thin, with brown mustard.
Flaky pastry around Idahos mashed with slow fried onion, egg washed and baked golden.
Clear golden chicken broth, carrot and dill, one big light dumpling.
With a sour pickle and slaw. Rye, white or a club roll.
Cream cheese, sour cream and lemon zest on a buttery crumb crust, baked slow in a water bath.
Never leaves Manhattan. We need the eggs.
Soft cake cookie, iced half vanilla, half chocolate.
Cream cheese dough rolled with apricot jam, walnuts and cinnamon sugar.
Best knish in Manhattan, and I grew up under a roller coaster. Ask for Max.
Cucumber, lime, mint and honey blended and strained, poured over ice and topped with seltzer.
Chocolate syrup and cold milk, hit hard with seltzer.
Bottomless at the counter. Tea comes in a glass.
No sneezing near the bake case.
